## RCA — confirmed root cause (Phase 1 complete)

**Mechanism.** `compact_trigger._rebar_dir` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:48-50`)
derives every compaction sidecar as `os.path.dirname(tracker) + "/.rebar"` with NO symlink
resolution. A `make worktree` worktree's `.tickets-tracker` is a SYMLINK to the canonical
store while its `.rebar` is a real per-worktree directory, so `dirname()` stops at the
worktree and all three sidecars are keyed on the CALLER, not the store. Confirmed against the
existing contract `_store/lock.canonical_tracker` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py:150-153`):
"Resolve to a canonical path ... so symlinked and real-path callers contend on the SAME lock
file." The sibling `.rebar/hlc.lock` already resolves internally (`_store/hlc.py:80-83`), and
`_proc.detached_child_cwd` documents this exact worktree-symlink hazard.

**Runtime proof (dynamic claims, observed executing — not read off the source).** Two worktree
views of one canonical store, driven through the real functions:

```
lock path A      : <tmp>/wt-a/.rebar/compact-worker.lock
lock path B      : <tmp>/wt-b/.rebar/compact-worker.lock
paths equal      : False
acquire A        : True
acquire B        : 4          <-- BOTH held the "one compactor at a time" lock at once
canonical .rebar : <absent>   <-- nothing was ever created on the store
stale in B after A stamped a sweep : True   <-- B sees a store that has never swept
log path A       : <tmp>/wt-a/.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log
```

The exclusion the lock exists to provide does not hold: the second acquire returned a live fd
instead of `None`. That result also discriminates against the two rival explanations — that
`os.path.dirname` already normalises a symlinked path, and that the lock was store-scoped by
some other route — both of which predict `None` and a canonical lock file.

**Live evidence on this host:** 33 worktree-local `.rebar/compact-sweep.stamp` files and 33
worktree-local `.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log` files, and ZERO shared `compact-worker.lock`.
Every one of those stamps is a worktree that re-fires a store-wide sweep the store just had.

**What each artifact protects (established before moving any of them):**
* `compact-worker.lock` — mutual exclusion of compactor PROCESSES over one store
  (`:40` "one compactor at a time"). The proposition is about the store. Store-scoped.
* `compact-sweep.stamp` — written only by `compact.compact_all_cli` (`compact.py:617-622`)
  after a sweep of the shared tracker, and read by `_sweep_is_stale` to answer "does this
  STORE need a sweep". Nothing in the proposition mentions the worktree. Store-scoped, and
  its worktree-locality has the extra behavioural consequence the lock does not: a fresh
  worktree always reads maximally stale and re-fires a redundant store-wide sweep.
* `logs/compact-worker.log` — stderr of a detached child that sweeps the store and outlives
  the worktree that spawned it. Gitignored local diagnostics, but about the store; scattering
  it across removable worktrees destroys the only record of a failed sweep. Store-scoped.

No artifact here turned out to be genuinely per-worktree state.

**Legitimacy: `defect`.** The behaviour violates a cited design invariant stated in the code
itself (`:40` "one compactor at a time") and the store's explicit `canonical_tracker`
contract. Not a feature request: nothing new is being added, only the resolution that makes
the existing artifacts address what they were written to address.

**Defect origin — `caused_by` 1fde-becd-942a-4351 (gaudy-gangrenous-basilisk).**
`git blame -w -C -M -L 47,62` on the implicated lines names exactly one commit,
`d2dea317ec9405900c6769d8912e64b4624bfaf5` (2026-08-13, "Trigger compaction from the close,
out of band"), which ADDED the whole file — `rebar-ticket: 1fde-becd-942a-4351`. Date test
applied: `canonical_tracker` has existed since 57114212cf01 (2026-06-12), two months BEFORE
the implicated lines, so this is not an unmet obligation created by a later change — the
consumer failed an already-existing contract at birth, and there is no earlier point at which
the behaviour was right. Class: `plan_defect` — the derivation was copied verbatim from
`enrich_drain` ("as the drain uses"), inheriting the drain's missing resolution along with the
machinery it meant to reuse, and a reviewer of that story could have caught it.

**One correction to this ticket's description:** it states that `rebar doctor` "describes the
canonical `compact-worker.lock`". It does not — `doctor_locks.scan_locks` canonicalises
(`doctor_locks.py:328-329`) but its leg list is
`tickets-write-fcntl / tickets-write-mkdir / hlc / enrich-drain` (`doctor_locks.py:90-93`);
there is no compact-worker leg. The canonicalisation is still good evidence of the
store-scoped convention, but doctor does not currently report this lock at all. Not fixed
here (adding a doctor leg would be new capability, not restoration).
